title_en: Chen Sunming — procuratorial protest case for causing a traffic accident
keywords_en: criminal; traffic accident; retrial; Supreme People's Court; Fujian Province; natural person; criminal law; determination of subjective fault; distinction between intentional homicide and causing a traffic accident; affirm the original judgment; drunk driving; driving in reverse direction at high speed to break through a checkpoint; hitting and killing an on-duty armed police officer; intentional homicide
full_text_en:
Chen Sunming — Protest against Traffic Accident Judgment

Protesting Authority: Supreme People's Procuratorate of the People's Republic of China.

Defendant: Chen Sunming, male, born on August 27, 1975, a farmer from Jinjiang City, Fujian Province. Arrested on August 29, 1994.

Defense Counsel: Tu Mingzhong, lawyer from Qingyuan Law Firm, Quanzhou, Fujian Province.

The Supreme People's Procuratorate of the People's Republic of China, considering that the final judgment of Fujian High People's Court in the case of Chen Sunming for causing a traffic accident was indeed erroneous, filed a protest with the Supreme People's Court of the People's Republic of China on December 27, 1998, in accordance with the provisions of Article 205, paragraph 3 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

In this case, the Quanzhou Intermediate People's Court of Fujian Province originally rendered a first-instance judgment on September 24, 1996: Chen Sunming was convicted of the crime of causing casualties by dangerous driving methods and sentenced to death, with deprivation of political rights for life. Fujian High People's Court rendered a final judgment on May 30, 1997: set aside the criminal judgment of Quanzhou Intermediate People's Court; Chen Sunming was convicted of the crime of causing a traffic accident and sentenced to seven years' imprisonment.

The Supreme People's Procuratorate was of the opinion that the conduct of the defendant at first instance, Chen Sunming, constituted the crime of intentional homicide, and that the Fujian High People's Court's characterization of Chen Sunming's offense was incorrect and the sentence was inappropriately lenient. The reasons were:

1. The defendant at first instance, Chen Sunming, knew that there were duty officers conducting inspections at the toll station. To evade inspection, he turned into the wrong-way lane, accelerated, and forcibly rushed through the barrier, causing the armed police soldier You Xiliang, who was performing inspection duties ahead, to be struck and killed. Chen Sunming knew that his conduct could cause the harmful consequence of the victim's death, but he adopted an attitude of indifference, resulting in the victim's death. His conduct already constituted the crime of intentional homicide. Therefore, Fujian High People's Court's characterization as the crime of causing a traffic accident was erroneous.

2. The conduct of the defendant at first instance, Chen Sunming, caused serious consequences and had a detrimental impact, and should be severely punished according to law.

The Supreme People's Court, upon trial, found the following facts:

At about 8:00 p.m. on July 19, 1994, the defendant at first instance, Chen Sunming, drank alcohol together with five other persons at the Southern Dance Hall in Quanzhou. Chen Sunming drank several cans of "Blue Ribbon" beer. At about 2:00 a.m. the following day, Chen Sunming drove an unlicensed Suzuki 250C motorcycle at a speed of over 80 kilometers per hour back to Jinjiang City, passing through the Shunji Bridge Toll Station in Quanzhou.

The Shunji Bridge Toll Station in Quanzhou had east and west lanes, each 6.8 meters wide. Between the two lanes and on both outer sides, there were three inspection zones extending 32 meters north-south along the lanes, with ticket booths at the northern and southern ends of each inspection zone.

That night, several armed police soldiers and toll station staff were inspecting smuggled vehicles at the Shunji Bridge Toll Station. When Chen Sunming approached the toll station from north to south, he saw vehicles being inspected at the southbound exit. Fearing that his unlicensed motorcycle would be confiscated, he intended to forcibly pass through the east wrong-way lane, which was then empty of vehicles and persons. When the motorcycle was still 45 meters from the northern end of the toll station, the toll station staff noticed that Chen was about to rush through and shouted loudly, signaling him to stop. Chen did not stop, but continued to drive at over 80 km/h in the wrong direction through the eastern lane, passing the northern ticket booth. When the motorcycle was about 20 meters from the southern ticket booth, armed police soldier You Xiliang and others, who were standing near the ticket booth on the outer side of the southbound exit of the western lane, heard the shouts and ran from that location toward the eastern lane to intercept Chen Sunming, who was rushing through. You ran eastward for about 10 meters, then collided head-on with the motorcycle approaching at high speed in the wrong lane, at a point about 2 meters outside the southern ticket booth, in the middle of the east lane's southbound entrance. Chen Sunming and the motorcycle slid to the ground for over 30 meters, and Chen immediately lost consciousness. You Xiliang, after being struck by the motorcycle, was dragged southward for over 10 meters, hit the guardrail at the roadside, and then bounced back onto the road. You Xiliang was sent to the hospital for emergency treatment but died at about 3:00 a.m. Forensic examination determined that You Xiliang died from shock caused by multiple soft tissue injuries throughout the body, skull base fracture with hemorrhage, and comminuted fractures of the left femur and left tibia and fibula due to impact from a blunt object.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence:

1. Testimony of witnesses Wu Hongsheng, Yang Laisheng, Li Yubo, and others, confirming that the defendant Chen Sunming drove a motorcycle at a high speed of approximately 80 kilometers per hour, and despite being shouted at and signaled to stop, forcibly rushed through in the wrong-way lane. You Xiliang, upon hearing the shouts, ran from a point more than 10 meters away from the centerline of the wrong-way lane and was struck in the middle of that lane. Testimony of witness Jiang Zhaoxu confirmed that before the incident, his colleague was driving a motorcycle at about 70 kilometers per hour approaching the bridge north of the toll station when Chen Sunming overtook from behind at high speed. When the colleague reached the middle of the bridge, Chen's motorcycle was already more than 200 meters ahead. At that time, the engine sound of Chen's motorcycle was very loud, but whether Chen accelerated before rushing through the barrier could not be confirmed. The witness stated that just as his shout for Chen to stop ended, Chen's motorcycle had already passed the northern ticket booth of the toll station. This testimony confirmed that the speed of Chen Sunming's motorcycle exceeded 70 kilometers per hour.

2. Autopsy report, confirming that the victim You Xiliang died from shock caused by impact from a blunt object, resulting in multiple soft tissue injuries throughout the body, skull base fracture with hemorrhage, and comminuted fractures of the left femur and left tibia and fibula.

3. Traffic accident scene investigation records and photographs, confirming the model of the motorcycle driven by the defendant Chen Sunming, the route Chen Sunming took on the wrong-way lane, and the location where the victim was struck.

4. Multiple confessions by the defendant Chen Sunming that he drove after drinking alcohol, and fearing that his motorcycle would be confiscated, he rushed through the barrier at high speed in the wrong direction, causing You Xiliang's death.

The Supreme People's Court held that:

The key issue in this case is whether, with respect to the serious consequence of You Xiliang's death resulting from the high-speed motorcycle rushing through the barrier, the defendant Chen Sunming subjectively had an attitude of indifference, or had a negligent attitude of failing to foresee what should have been foreseen or lightly believing it could be avoided. To determine the subjective culpability of Chen Sunming, a specific analysis must be made based on the specific circumstances at the time.

Upon consultation with the traffic management department, it was indicated that: From the time a driver notices a situation requiring a stop to the time of braking to a halt, generally about 2 seconds are needed. The normal human reaction time parameter is 1.25 seconds, meaning 0.5 seconds for the eyes to perceive a target and transmit the signal to the brain, and 0.75 seconds for the brain to react and for the hands and feet to take braking action. This is only a parameter and is affected by factors such as skill proficiency and reaction ability. If alcohol has been consumed, reaction ability is relatively slower.

At the time of the incident, the armed police soldiers on duty and the toll station staff were all standing on the steps of the ticket booths. The defendant Chen Sunming, to evade inspection, intended to forcibly pass through the east wrong-way lane, which was then empty of vehicles and persons. You Xiliang ran from a point more than 10 meters away to the point of impact after hearing the shouts. At that time, Chen Sunming was driving a motorcycle at high speed, with his attention focused ahead. Additionally, due to the obstruction of the ticket booths within the toll station, his field of vision was relatively narrow, and Chen could not see You Xiliang's movements.

When the toll station staff signaled the defendant Chen Sunming to stop, the motorcycle was 45 meters from the north entrance of the station. The total length of the Shunji Bridge Toll Station was 32 meters. The point where the victim You Xiliang was struck was 2 meters outside the south entrance of the station. The total distance of these three segments was 79 meters. At that time, the motorcycle driven by Chen Sunming was traveling at a speed of over 80 kilometers per hour. Even calculated at 80 kilometers per hour, the motorcycle would travel 22 meters per second, and the time required to traverse the 79-meter distance would be 3.5 seconds. Each motor vehicle lane at the toll station was 6.8 meters wide, and the point of impact was in the middle of the east lane, 3.4 meters from the roadside. The minimum distance for You Xiliang to run from the outer side of the west lane, across the west lane, to the middle of the east lane was 10.2 meters. Based on a normal person's running speed, the time required for You Xiliang to cover this distance was 2 seconds. If the time when the toll station staff shouted to stop is taken as the starting point, by the time You Xiliang ran to the point of impact, Chen Sunming was only 1.5 seconds of driving distance away. Under such circumstances, even if Chen Sunming had taken braking measures immediately after spotting You Xiliang, a collision would have been unavoidable. If further consideration is given to the fact that Chen Sunming had consumed alcohol that evening, reducing his reaction ability and relatively prolonging reaction time, or that You Xiliang did not immediately run toward the point of impact upon hearing the shouts, then Chen Sunming's braking reaction distance would be even shorter, and the collision even more unavoidable.

In summary, it can be determined that: The defendant Chen Sunming's act of rushing through the barrier by driving on the wrong-way lane, which was then empty of vehicles and persons, was intentional; the intent was to evade inspection and impoundment of the motorcycle. Chen Sunming could not have foreseen at that time that You Xiliang would suddenly appear on the wrong-way lane to intercept him. After he spotted You, the speed and distance had already made the collision unavoidable. Therefore, it cannot be determined that Chen Sunming subjectively had knowledge of or an indifferent mental state regarding the serious consequence of causing You Xiliang's death before it occurred.

The defendant at first instance, Chen Sunming, violated traffic regulations by driving a motorcycle at high speed after consuming alcohol and, to evade inspection, drove in the wrong direction and rushed through the barrier, thereby causing the serious consequence of the death of an armed police soldier on duty who suddenly ran to the middle of the road to intercept an illegal driving act. His conduct constituted the crime of causing a traffic accident, and the circumstances were particularly egregious. Fujian High People's Court's conviction and sentencing of Chen Sunming under Article 113 of the Criminal Law of 1979 were not improper and should be affirmed. The protest ground of the Supreme People's Procuratorate that Chen Sunming's conduct constituted the crime of intentional homicide cannot be established and is not adopted. Accordingly, the Supreme People's Court, in accordance with Article 206, Article 193, and Article 189(1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on June 17, 1999, ruled as follows:

Affirmed the criminal judgment No. (1996) Min Xing Zhong Zi No. 675 of Fujian High People's Court.
